messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are still at their posts—but the paint’s peeling in places, and no one’s rushing to fix it. The kids are talking louder in the streets, and the old men are finally nailing down their roofs. For now, the machine hums along, but the gears aren’t as tight as they used to be."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are holding, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—even the loyalists are starting to whisper about back doors. The machine’s still running, but it’s running hot, and no one’s sure how long the fuel will last."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different—like the old guard is holding its breath, not celebrating. The jokes are sharper, the traders are sweating, and the usual speeches sound like they’re reading from a script they don’t believe in. Could be the calm before the storm… or the last gasp before the collapse. Either way, we should be ready for the wind to change."*"
Sender 4: "*"The machine’s still running, but it’s coughing—no one’s pulling the plug yet, but the mechanics are watching the gauges a little too closely. The real question isn’t if something breaks, but whether anyone’s left who knows how to fix it before the whole thing stalls out."*"
Sender 5: "*"Things seem quiet on the surface—too quiet. The usual signs of trouble aren’t there, but the garbage isn’t getting picked up on time, and the foreigners are watching like hawks. Let’s keep our ears open, but no sudden moves—this isn’t the moment."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no panic. But the air feels different now, like the quiet before something shifts. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the calm before something shifts. The jokes are sharper, the queues move slower, and the top is still making moves, but you can hear the gears grinding. We’re not there yet, but the ground’s softer than it looks."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm brewing, more like the moment before a dam starts to crack. The cracks are small, but they’re there, and the water’s been rising for a while. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for safety."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—especially when the same whispers keep showing up in different places. The regime’s holding for now, but the way the money’s moving and the way the security forces are acting tells me this isn’t just business as usual. Stay sharp, but don’t let anyone see you looking too closely."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different—like the moment before a storm, but no one’s sure if it’ll break or just blow over. The usual channels are holding, but the jokes are getting louder, and the inner circle’s grip feels tighter than ever. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could still go either way."*"
Sender 11: "*"The usual faces are keeping their distance, but the kitchen staff is whispering about extra supplies being moved out of town—just in case. The kids in the park aren’t even pretending to look away when the patrols pass anymore. Nothing’s breaking yet, but the air feels like it does before a storm when you know the roof might not hold."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels lighter in some corners, but the walls are still standing—just a few cracks, nothing that can’t be patched for now. The kids came home the same as always, and the bills keep getting paid, but the foreigners are packing their bags quietly. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t over, just… breathing."*"
Sender 13: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but the cracks are showing—elites are still talking to each other, but the air’s thinner than it was last month. The streets are patchy—some places humming, others dead quiet—and the business crowd’s playing it safe, not panicking, but not betting big either. Keep your circles tight, but don’t assume the quiet means calm. We’ll know more when the next shoe drops."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels different—like the quiet before something shifts. Not a storm yet, but the wind’s picking up, and the usual rules don’t seem to apply anymore. Keep your heads down, but stay ready—just in case."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels different—like the ground is shifting underfoot, even if no one’s admitting it yet. The guards at the checkpoints are laughing too loud, the warehouses are full but the doors are unlocked, and even the newspapers can’t keep their own lies straight. Still, no one’s sure if this is the calm before the storm or just the quiet before another long wait—but for the first time, people are asking *what happens next* instead of *if* it happens. Stay sharp, stay safe, and keep your ears open. We’ll talk soon."*"
Sender 16: "*"Things feel quieter than they should—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting to see if the new cabinet holds or if the cracks just got papered over. The streets are grumbling, but no one’s reaching for matches yet… though the fact that the airlines are adding flights says more than the news does."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the wind. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there, and the question is whether they’ll hold or split open. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could be the calm before something, but we don’t know what."*"
Sender 18: "*"Something’s shifting—people are moving quietly, but the regime’s grip feels tighter in the strangest ways. The fixer’s gone, the hospitals are running dry, and the money men are nervous, but the deal with the foreigners is still being sold as a win. Keep your ears open, but don’t trust the silence—it’s never just quiet."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the whole thing coming down or just the paint peeling—yet. The old guard’s still holding the reins, but the horses are getting restless, and the stable hands are whispering to each other. Keep your ears open, but don’t bet on anything just yet."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the ground shifting underfoot. The usual cracks are showing, but the real question is whether anyone’s watching them *or* just waiting to see who stumbles first. Stay sharp, but don’t let the quiet fool you—something’s moving, even if we can’t see it yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s sure if it’s the calm before something or just another slow week. The usual signs are there, but nothing’s breaking yet. Still, the smart money’s on things staying the same… for now. Keep your ears open, but don’t move until we see which way the wind’s really blowing."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels heavier than the news would suggest—like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending it’s just another Tuesday. The walls are still standing, but the cracks? They’re not where you’d expect."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the foundation or just the paint. The regime’s still standing tall in public, but the whispers in the backrooms are getting louder—and the money’s already walking out the door. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The moment’s coming, but we don’t know which way it’ll break."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different now—not like before, when we were just waiting for something to happen, but like we’re all holding our breath for the same moment. The cracks are there, but no one’s sure yet if they’ll split wide open or just settle back into place—so we keep our eyes open, our voices steady, and our plans ready, just in case."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels lighter than it did last month—people are talking more, reaching out—but don’t mistake that for safety. The banks are tightening, the schools are quiet, and the regime’s still playing catch-up with its own story. If the wrong person stumbles, this could shift fast. Stay sharp, but keep it quiet."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
